commits.message:
Skip blank and all-zero identity grant ids in GrantStrategy

sanitizeIdentityGrants calls insert(2, "-") on every id; a blank id (or
one that strips to under 2 chars, e.g. K00) throws
StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and the grant task fails for the whole
person, so none of their articles get grant evidence. 53 prod identities
carry such ids (mer2005, cap4010 hit it in prod on 2026-09-23).

commits.author: paulalbert1
commits.message:
Patch userAssertion on the stored Analysis when the gold standard is written (#752)

The curate tabs render userAssertion from the stored Analysis, which a
gold-standard write never touched; an accept stayed under Suggested until
something re-ran the feature generator for that person. After either
/reciter/goldstandard handler saves, read the gold standard back, set
userAssertion per stored article (rejected wins, as in
Analysis.performAnalysis), and save the Analysis the way the feature
generator does. No retrieval, no re-score. Best effort: a failure logs and
the next feature-generator run converges as before.

commits.author: paulalbert1
commits.message:
Address review: iterate a sorted key snapshot, guard the removal, test the rules by value

- Walk a copied key list and look values up as we go, so a name already
  dropped is never used as the "full" name that drops others.
- Sort the snapshot fullest-name-first (then toString) so the survivor of a
  symmetric rule-3 pair never depends on HashMap iteration order.
- Replace the early return with a guard on the removal itself.
- Rule 3 comment corrected: it is a case-only duplicate check; a middle
  initial is not collapsed into a full middle name (pre-#704 behaviour).
- Rename idenityAuthorNames -> identityAuthorNames.
- Tests: assert which names survive, not just how many; feed alc4061's
  shape through sanitizeIdentityAuthorNames end-to-end; prove production
  mixes "" and null middle names; pin the rule-3 survivor with a
  LinkedHashMap; cover empty/partial names.

commits.author: paulalbert1
commits.message:
Decide name-variant removals over a snapshot instead of mutating through live iterators

checkToIgnoreNameVariants walked the identity's name-variant map with two live
iterators inside a nested loop, and three separate blocks in the same pass could
each call remove(). When a removed entry was the iterator's last, the 'advance
past it' guard had nothing to advance to, and the next block's remove() threw
IllegalStateException — a 500 on every feature-generator call for any identity
whose variants matched two rules in one pass. alc4061 is one: primary
'Alberto Mario' with an empty middle name, alternates 'Alberto Mario' / null and
'Alberto' / null. His 09-02 accept sat under Suggested for twelve days because
neither the nightly run nor the curate page's Refresh could get past it.

The three rules are unchanged, lifted into isNameVariantToIgnore(full, candidate):
same last name and (1) full's first name starts with candidate's and neither has
a middle name, (2) same prefix and candidate's middle name is blank, or (3) all
three parts equal ignoring case. The loop now decides over a snapshot of the
entries and removes from the map by key, never below one remaining name.

Closes #704.

commits.author: paulalbert1
commits.message:
Merge incremental ESearchResult upserts instead of replacing them

An incremental run's pmid list is only that night's window. upsertedStrategyEntry
substituted it for the stored block whenever the stored block was not itself
ALL_PUBLICATIONS, so a strategy's pmid list shrank to whatever that one window
returned. initializeEngineParameters builds the scoring candidate set as the union
of these blocks, so every dropped pmid vanished from the person's scoring input --
while the article stayed in the PubMedArticle cache and in PmidProvenance, making
the loss invisible.

Measured on prod 2026-09-05: 1,446 authorship_review rows had lost their pmid this
way, 1,445 of them behind a block whose stored lookupType was already incremental.
A within-person paired control put the loss rate at 67% behind an incremental block
versus 0% behind a full sweep, and it was still accruing -- 388 destructive block
rewrites dated that day.

Now any incoming entry that is not a genuine ALL_PUBLICATIONS sweep merges into the
stored list. A real full sweep still replaces wholesale: it is authoritative, it is
what prunes pmids the person's queries no longer match, and it bounds the merged
list's growth against the 400KB item cap (#640-B). The existing #696/E13 rule is
unchanged -- when the stored entry is ALL_PUBLICATIONS the merged entry keeps that
marker and the sweep's retrievalDate.

This also covers the swallowed-429 case: a strategy returning zero articles tonight
no longer erases what it found before.

Size bound checked against prod rather than assumed. Over a 1,500-uid sample the
worst case -- every strategy holding the entire per-person pmid union, which does
not actually happen since strategies retrieve different sets -- peaks at 87% of the
400KB cap and 0 of 1,500 exceed it.

Tests: incrementalOverIncrementalReplacesTheEntry asserted the old behaviour and is
replaced by incrementalOverIncrementalMergesRatherThanReplacing, plus coverage for
the empty window, deduplication, and full-sweep pruning. mvn -o test 374/374 pass.
Reverting the guard with the tests unchanged fails exactly the 3 new merge tests
(expected <[1, 2, 3]> but was <[]>), so they are load-bearing.

commits.author: paulalbert1
commits.message:
Stop labelling a first-name prefix match as full-exact (#746)

ScoreByNameStrategy reported nameMatchFirstType=full-exact on three branches that only established a prefix or suffix relationship, not equality. A byline of "Shuofei" was therefore indistinguishable from a genuine exact match against a registered "Shuo": the compensating identitySubstringOfArticle-firstName modifier (-1.608) lands in a different feature, so nothing downstream could tell the two apart.

Three honest buckets replace the over-claim, each with its own property defaulting to the full-exact value (1.852):
  full-prefix              registered first name (>=2 chars) begins the byline first name
  full-suffix              registered first name (>=2 chars) ends it (Cary -> MCary)
  inferredInitials-prefix  registered first name is a single letter that begins the byline
                           first name ('M.' -> Mayra); semantically an initial match, whose
                           correct score is inferredInitials-exact (0.441)

No predicate changes. The single-letter class gets its own branch rather than a length guard on the prefix branch, because a guard would drop those rows through to full-conflictingAllButInitials (-2.646) -- worse than the status quo and a numeric change.

Verified numerically inert. An 11,520-case enumeration of both first-name cascades, run against the pre-change source and this branch, shows 776 label changes and zero differences in nameMatchFirstScore, nameMatchMiddleScore, nameMatchLastScore, nameMatchModifierScore or nameScoreTotal; nameMatchMiddleType and nameMatchModifier are unchanged everywhere.

Requires ReCiter---Scoring #23 to be deployed first: nameMatchFirstType is not only a diagnostic string, it feeds nameMatchTypeOrdinal, a numeric feature in both deployed models. Shipping this alone moves 34 of 48,337 measured article-rows, worst -18.02 points.
